 BUNCOMBE COUNTY, N.C. (WLOS) — With thousands of Buncombe County residents facing Medicare plan changes next year, a local nonprofit is offering a free class to help seniors navigate their coverage options online as demand for counseling grows.
 An analysis of federal Medicare data by Medicare On Main found that 11 Medicare Advantage plans offered in Buncombe County in 2026 will no longer be available locally in 2027. At least 2,064 residents were enrolled in those plans as of September, though not all will necessarily need to select replacement coverage.
 “Even if they don’t make changes, the plan makes changes,” said Sue Adams, a longtime volunteer with the Council on Aging of Buncombe County. 
 The changes are raising concerns about higher health care costs and a growing digital divide that local counselors say is making it harder for some seniors to compare coverage options.
 WHO QUALIFIES FOR $90 MEDICARE PAYMENT, AND WHY MILLIONS WILL NOT RECEIVE IT 
 According to the Council on Aging, some Medicare plans are increasing premiums, copays and deductibles next year, potentially putting additional financial pressure on seniors living on fixed incomes.
 “If they have a big increase in their health care costs, whether that be for the drug plan or their co-pays for their Medicare Advantage go up, it really makes a big impact on their budget,” Adams said.
 Jennifer Jacobs, Medicare manager at the Council on Aging, said rising medical and prescription drug costs are adding pressure as seniors review their coverage options.
 Meanwhile, the nonprofit said its Medicare counseling appointments are already full in Buncombe and Henderson counties, with counselors working from a waitlist.
 HAYWOOD COUNTY RESIDENTS RETHINK HEALTH CARE COVERAGE AFTER PREMIUM INCREASE 
 But finding affordable coverage is only part of the challenge. As more Medicare resources move online, Jacobs said some older adults are struggling to navigate the websites needed to compare prescription drug coverage, participating doctors and available plans.
 “Just finding information, searching for plans, all of that’s very confusing to people that are not so tech savvy,” Jacobs said.
 To address that digital divide, the Council on Aging is helping offer Medicare.gov education in partnership with North Carolina’s Seniors’ Health Insurance Information Program and Land of Sky Regional Council’s WestNGN initiative.
 Regular Medicare open enrollment ends Dec. 7, with coverage changes taking effect Jan. 1, 2027. Residents whose Medicare Advantage plans are not renewed may qualify for a special enrollment period through Feb. 28, 2027.
 The free class will provide hands-on assistance with creating Medicare.gov accounts, entering medications and preferred pharmacies, checking health care providers and comparing coverage options. Medicare counselors and technical advisers will be available to answer questions.
 It is scheduled for Nov. 14 from 10 to 11:30 a.m. at Groce United Methodist Church, 954 Tunnel Road, in Asheville.
